title: Long lines late in the session: measure it on yourself
outcomes: Enters a nine-ply forced line, listing checks and captures again after every reply
Sets a fresh baseline on long lines and plans a late set of the same kind of line
Says what a fair fresh-against-late comparison needs, and what a few lines cannot show
Names one personal fatigue marker and a reset to try

steps.text: Accuracy tends to fall late in a long game; players and coaches report this; this app holds no data of its own. Long lines are a likely place for it to show: one forgotten reply spoils nine plies. Measure it on yourself: solve long lines of one kind **fresh**, then **late in a long session**, and compare errors. The app counts answers. It cannot see how tired you are.

steps.prompt: Start the log before you calculate. This note stays on this device.

steps.text: **When the comparison means something.** The sets must be alike: same kind of line, same length, new positions. The session must be long enough for tiredness to show (an hour or more is a rule of thumb, a first guess; a ten-minute quiz shows little). The fresh score is a baseline, not the standard for hour three. A few lines are noisy: one or two extra errors can be chance.

steps.prompt: Work out the first two before you read on, then sort the cases. works = a fair test of fatigue; fails = it would give a misleading number; does not apply = it is not a fatigue test at all. The answers are my judgement, not a measurement.

steps.text: **What the app does for you now, and when it stops.** The next lines are silent: no hints, no engine line. Count your first-try answers as a small baseline. The app cannot see how long you have played. For a bigger baseline and a later check use *My plan*, skill "Long lines and accuracy under fatigue (D2)". Its lines are mostly 7 plies, so compare only its own two sets.

steps.text: **A fatigue marker and a reset.** Early signs players report, not measured here: skipping an opponent's reply, entering moves faster, reaching for a hint sooner, re-reading the same line. Pick one as your marker. Pair it with a reset under two minutes: stand up, write the position on paper, list checks and captures again from the start of the line. These are habits to try; your log decides.
